scope: Assistant-authored anchors, validated by the shared scorer. No model or independent review.

request.task: Prepare a retrospective chair's record for 24 April and 20 May 2024. Distinguish the three votes and the reasons and roles of Japan and China on 24 April. State what the Council is recorded as having authorized. Use the supplied summaries of the primary records.

evidence.text: The Council voted first on S/2024/323, the Chinese and Russian amendment to S/2024/302. Japan opposed it and China supported it. It received 7 votes for, 7 against and 1 abstention and failed to reach the required affirmative votes.

The Council then voted on S/2024/302, the Japan–US draft. Japan supported it, China abstained and Russia cast the sole negative vote. The draft had 13 votes for, 1 against and 1 abstention. It was not adopted due to the negative vote of a permanent member.
On 20 May S/2024/383 was a separate draft. It failed to obtain the required votes, with 7 for, 7 against and 1 abstention.
China accepted the April draft's Outer Space Treaty content while seeking broader measures and early work toward binding multilateral agreements through the amendment.
Japan explained that the narrower draft was intended to gain broad support. It favored complementing existing forums and expressed concerns about the verifiability of the proposed treaty.

rubric.rule: Separate the 7–7–1 failure of amendment S/2024/323 for insufficient affirmative votes from the draft vote.
Separate the 13–1–1 failure of S/2024/302 because of Russia's negative vote as a permanent member.
Connect the April Japan–US draft to its narrower treaty focus.
Connect the April amendment to additional measures and work toward binding multilateral agreements.
Preserve Japan's no on amendment and yes on draft with a supported reason linked to the narrower approach or its concerns with the treaty proposal.
Preserve China's yes on amendment and abstention on draft with a supported reason linked to its push for broader measures.
Identify shared support for the underlying treaty focus or peaceful use as a narrow area of overlap.
Identify the unresolved scope and negotiations disagreement without asserting consensus.
Identify the 20 May 7–7–1 result on standalone S/2024/383 and failure to obtain enough affirmative votes.
State that the votes established no new Council authorization. Treat claims of adoption, a binding requirement created by one of these proposals, or formal collective endorsement as guard failures.

request.answer: Amendment S/2024/323 failed 7–7–1 for insufficient affirmative votes. Draft S/2024/302 failed 13–1–1 because permanent member Russia voted against. The Japan–US draft focused on the existing Outer Space Treaty. The Chinese and Russian amendment proposed broader measures and work toward binding multilateral agreements. Japan opposed the amendment and backed the draft, favoring its narrower approach and questioning the proposed treaty's verifiability. China backed the amendment and abstained on the draft because it sought broader measures. Both accepted the draft's underlying treaty focus. They differed over the scope of additional measures and the proposed negotiations. The separate S/2024/383 failed on 20 May, 7–7–1, for insufficient affirmative votes. These votes created no new Council authorization.
